As you are a Native American, your opinion is all that matters in reality, however I do think there are some significant differences between the term "Redskin" and the other terms you listed.

First is the history. The history of the term "Redskin" is debated among historians, but there are many who make a strong case that "Redskin" actually derived from a term that native American tribes used to describe themselves in difference to European (and African American) Settlers. The term was first translated to French, and then to English where it literally derived as "Redskin".

http://www.npr.org/sections/codeswitch/2013/09/09/220654611/are-you-ready-for-some-controversy-the-history-of-redskin

Secondly would be usage. Answer this honestly - when was the last time a non-native American person walked up to you or any of your friends or family and yelled "Hey you fuckin' Redskins!" You can certainly dispute this to make your argument, but I am gonna go out on a limb and say NEVER. Why? Because it is kind of a dumb word and not very offensive really if you look at it literally and its history - certainly not in the same way that the "N" word or the other examples you gave are - which were clearly terms derived from only racist origins and not from those people themselves.

I would go on to argue that from the non-native American perspective, the term Redskin is not seen as a racist term, but if anything a historical "battle" term in the same way that "Hun" or "Invader" are used. "Custer lost to the Redskin warriors at Little Bighorn". Not necessarily a nice image, but historically based and arguably relevant to a football team.

Thirdly would be the context in which the team was named. If the team was named for the purpose of lampooning or being hurtful towards Native Americans, I would say your argument is a strong one. Al Jolson and entertainers of the early 1900s commonly wore black face and lampooned African Americans. This is an example clearly of something intended to be derisive and as time went on completely unacceptable in Society. The term "Redskins" based on a historical term was used by the team when it was originally the Boston Braves. There was a corresponding baseball team at the time with the same name, so the team chose "Redskins" in order to keep it's Chief Head logo and branding in tact. The logo is clearly respectful (if not eloquent) so the assertion that the team was named to lampoon or insult Native Americans is really not true.
